svg.title: Spur gear geometry basics and belt drive forces (example)
svg.text: Spur gear geometry (m = 2, z = 17 / 34, α = 20°) and belt drive forces (HTD 8M, T = 28.3 N·m)
Left: pitch, base, tip and root circles, line of action and contact length. Right: tight and slack side, pretension, shaft load. Guide 10 §22 and §23.
line of action, 20°, tangent to both base circles
da = d + 2m = 38 mm, df = d − 2.5m = 29 mm, db = d·cos α = 31.95 mm
z_min without undercut = 2/sin²α = 17.1 → z = 17 is the limit (use x > 0 or z ≥ 18)
Legend: tip circle (solid), pitch circle (red dash-dot), base circle (grey dash), root circle (thin)
n = 44 rpm (driver turns so the top strand moves ◀)
static pretension per strand F0 ≈ 0.5–0.7·Ft → 555 N (0.6)
shaft load at 180° wrap Fw ≈ 2·F0 = 1110 N
belt speed v = π·dw·n = 0.14 m/s (very low: static rating)
→ V-belt loads the bearings 27 % more and can slip; toothed belt keeps phase
Chain 08B (as built): F = T/r = 733 N, breaking 17.8 kN → static safety 24
values from guide 10 Part B · guide 10 · 2026-11-12
